narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>A square is five, so to multiply by five, add one square.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test it on eleven, which is two squares and a triangle. Adding a square gives sixteen.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Five times eleven is fifty five, so adding a square does not multiply at all.
removed_beats.on_screen: the hint card leaves; Chintu's bubble shows add one square; 2 squares and 1 triangle (11) gain one square and become 16; 11 × 5 = 55 is written beside it; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='before'/>To check, work out the value of the numeral before and after you move the symbols.
<bookmark mark='times'/>The new value should be exactly five times the old one, every time.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor and the answer card; two check lines appear: work out the number before and after; the after number should be five times the before number

old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu says to multiply by five, add one square. One square is worth five, so that adds five; it does not make the number five times as big.
